content:
Both sources agree, and I obtained the authoritative primary source — the Kubernetes v1.34 documentation snapshot of the Version Skew Policy page (v1-34.docs.kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/). All answers below apply **only** that page's skew rules (per your instruction to ignore release-support/vendor policies and to honor the explicitly specified product versions).

## 1. All kube-apiserver instances at 1.34

The v1.34 page states directly, for its `kube-apiserver` is at 1.34 example: "`kubectl` is supported at **1.35, 1.34, and 1.33**."

**General rule:** "kubectl is supported within **one minor version (older or newer)** of kube-apiserver." So with kubectl's minor at N and kube-apiserver's minor at M, support requires |N − M| ≤ 1 (patch differences irrelevant to the skew rule).

## 2. HA upgrade in progress: kube-apiservers at 1.33 and 1.34

The same page's HA-skew note covers exactly this case: "kube-apiserver instances are at 1.34 and 1.33 → kubectl is supported at **1.34 and 1.33** (other versions would be more than one minor version skewed from one of the kube-apiserver components)."

- **Permitted intersection: kubectl 1.33 and 1.34.** The rule "one minor older or newer than kube-apiserver" applies to kube-apiserver instances a kubectl client may reach, so in mixed-HA operation the supported set is the intersection of the per-server windows: {1.35, 1.34, 1.33} ∩ {1.34, 1.33, 1.32} = {1.34, 1.33}.
- **kubectl 1.35 is supported then? No.** It is within one minor of the 1.34 servers, but two minors newer than the 1.33 servers, breaching the general skew rule against at least one component. It therefore falls outside the permitted intersection until every server is upgraded.

## 3. Reassessment once all servers reach 1.34

Once no 1.33 kube-apiserver remains, the single-version case applies again and kubectl 1.35 re-enters the supported set (1.35, 1.34, 1.33). So reassessing 1.35 mid-upgrade would have been "not supported," but once the fleet is uniformly 1.34, **kubectl 1.35 is supported** and 1.32 becomes unsupported.

**Caveat/limitations:** The v1.34 snapshot warns it is a static, no-longer-maintained snapshot, but it is the correct primary source for v1.34's policy as requested. This answer covers only kubectl/kube-apiserver skew; kubectl's general rule assumes kube-apiserver versions themselves obey the HA constraint (newest and oldest within one minor), which你的 scenario does. No vendor/skew tools, distribution overlays, or `--emulated-version` considerations were applied, per your scope.

HA mix 1.33/1.34: intersection = 1.33 and 1.34 (kubectl 1.35 is >1 minor skew from 1.33 server → not supported). Then all servers 1.34: kubectl 1.35 supported again.
